M01.reason: Read FSM leaves ACK as soon as either the request is 0 or the write pointer is 0, so reads are released early and the flush check is bypassed; the read-side release timing and blocking during the software reset change.

M02.reason: This is the reset value of the ack retiming flop. It is only used when PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME=1, and the write FSM is in RUN right after reset, where the ack is ignored. The first clock edge reloads it with i_ack_rd before REQ or REL can read it, so no port can differ.

M03.reason: An accepted write no longer advances the write pointer, so o_full never asserts, stored words are overwritten and the read side never sees data.

M04.reason: When the pointers are equal the read-view occupancy becomes 2xDEPTH instead of 0, so o_empty and o_empty_thr are wrong.

M05.reason: With RETIME=0 the read side now sees the write pointer through an extra flop, so o_empty falls one cycle later than the exact model and gap-free streaming is lost.

M06.reason: The read pointer does not advance on an accepted read, so the same word is returned repeatedly and the occupancy never decreases.

M07.reason: The read-pointer clear condition is inverted, so the pointer is held at 0 in normal running and increments only in RST; reads return wrong data and the pointer is not reset by the software reset.

M08.reason: The write request flop is 1 in every state except HOLD, including RUN, so the read side is blocked permanently in normal operation and o_empty is stuck at 1.

M09.reason: The memory is written when i_wr_en is 0 and not when it is 1, so accepted words are not stored and read data is wrong.

M10.reason: When the next write pointer equals the read pointer the write-view occupancy becomes 2xDEPTH instead of 0, so o_full and o_full_thr are wrong when the FIFO is empty.

M11.reason: o_sw_rst_busy is inverted: it is 1 in normal running and 0 during the software reset sequence.

M12.reason: Reset value of the request retiming flop. With PARA_SFIFO_PTR_RETIME=1 the read side sees a request right after reset, blocks o_empty and spuriously runs the read reset FSM for a few cycles, delaying the first word. It is invisible only when RETIME=0.

M13.reason: The write FSM leaves REL when the ack is low or the read pointer is 0, instead of both. o_sw_rst_busy can fall before the read side has been flushed, which changes the busy timing and writes can resume early.

M14.reason: o_sw_rst_busy resets to 1 instead of 0, so it is 1 during hardware reset and o_full is forced to 1.

M15.reason: The wrap compare uses 2xDEPTH instead of 2xDEPTH-1, so the pointer wraps only by truncation. This breaks the modulo-2xDEPTH range for depths that are not a power of two (such as 5 or 12), giving wrong flags and addresses. It happens to be harmless for depth 8.

M16.reason: The read FSM goes RUN to RST when no request is visible, so reads are blocked and the pointer is cleared in normal operation and o_empty stays 1.

M17.reason: The read block term is inverted: reads are blocked in RUN and allowed during the software reset, so o_empty is stuck at 1 in normal operation.

M18.reason: The read pointer wrap compare uses 2xDEPTH instead of 2xDEPTH-1, so the wrap relies on truncation. Non-power-of-2 depths (such as 5 or 12) then get a wrong pointer range, occupancy and read address. It happens to be harmless for depth 8.

M19.reason: The ACK exit condition checks the visible write pointer is non-zero instead of zero, so the read side stays blocked after the software reset or is released at the wrong time.

M20.reason: The write pointer wrap condition is inverted, so the pointer is cleared or incremented at the wrong values and wraps incorrectly, corrupting address, order and full.

M21.reason: The reset branch is inverted, so the write-domain flops are held at reset values while i_rst_n_wr is high and run normally during reset.

M22.reason: With RETIME=0 the write FSM sees the read ack through an extra flop, so the REQ to PTR and REL to RUN transitions and the o_sw_rst_busy duration shift by one cycle.

M23.reason: o_underflow resets to 1 instead of 0, so it shows a pulse during hardware reset.

M24.reason: o_full_thr resets to 1 instead of 0, so it is 1 during hardware reset and until the first write clock edge after release.

M25.reason: The inverted compare yields the wrong memory read address for depths that are not a power of two (such as 5 or 12), so the wrong word is shown. For depth 8 the address truncation to LPARA_ADDR_W bits hides the change.

M34.reason: The read-domain reset branch is inverted, so read flops are held at reset values while i_rst_n_rd is high and run normally during reset.
